entities.summary: Imbert du Puy was a French cardinal who played a pivotal role in the papal politics of the 14th century. He was a nephew of Pope John XXII and was instrumental in shaping the Church's stance on the Avignon Papacy. Du Puy's significance lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the papal court and the French monarchy. His influence can be seen in the subsequent papal elections and the eventual return of the papacy to Rome. The French monarchy's reliance on du Puy's support led to a significant shift in the balance of power between the Church and the state. Du Puy's legacy extends beyond his political career, as he was also a patron of the arts and architecture, commissioning several notable works during his tenure as cardinal. The impact of his patronage can still be seen in the grand architecture of the French cathedrals and churches. Du Puy's story is a testament to the enduring power of patronage and the complex web of relationships that shape the course of history. As he once said, 'The Church is the backbone of Western civilization.'
